done_when: When a cold read or review loop stops, forge read, forge close, forge land and forge next print a ready-to-ask question that names the item in plain words and what it delivers, lists each open blocking note or finding as one plain sentence saying what goes wrong for whom, and says what accept, narrow and split would each concretely do for this item, and the guide tells the coordinator to ask exactly that

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The Done-when line requires one plain sentence per open blocker. `plain()` keeps two body sentences and appends them to the title. The close test expects one blocker to appear as “saving drops the basket. Returning shoppers lose their saved items.”, so the passing test confirms this unmet requirement. The proof-list note does not change the stated Done-when line; no allowance is recorded.
findings.title: Not done: blocker summaries still contain multiple sentences

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `read_question()` includes every non-advisory finding from the latest round without checking its disposition. After a third blocked read, a coordinator can mark one note `Disposition: cut` or `defer` before running `forge read` or `forge next`; both still present it as a problem for the owner to decide. The existing disposition rule treats those notes as settled (`story.py:729-737`), so the question no longer lists only open blocking notes.
findings.title: Not done: stopped reads list notes that have been resolved

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The question prints a fix's raw `why` and `done_when` as its name and delivery. Normal fixes may name a source location, and Forge itself creates follow-up fixes whose `why` contains a finding's `file:line` (`close.py:405-407`). If such a fix reaches a review stop, the owner gets that path and review jargon instead of the promised plain-words description. Only blocker text passes through `plain()`.
findings.title: Not done: stopped fix questions can show paths as the item name

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The proof list names `test_spec_reads_keep_full_scope.py::test_3` as proof that a later-round spec stop prints the question. Its changed assertion checks only the introductory line and the final `Next:` line; it never checks the question between them. Removing the question while retaining “in these words:” would leave this named proof passing. The other read test checks a spec question, but does not make this proof-list entry true.
findings.title: Not done: proof list claims a spec-question assertion the named test lacks

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: both findings are fixed in commit 715dee9; close re-reviews the current head

why: When a cold read or review loop stops, the owner is asked to accept, narrow or split with no context; with many items in parallel they can't tell what the item is or what was flagged
